feed.title: Subject: Eltoo / LN-Symmetry on Inquisition Signet: BIP 118 + 3-Round State Chain (APO+CTV)

entry.title: Subject: Eltoo / LN-Symmetry on Inquisition Signet: BIP 118 + 3-Round State Chain (APO+CTV)
entry.summary:
A recent experiment involved testing the CSFS+TH+IK script variant on signet after OP_TEMPLATEHASH became available. The scripts were adapted from Greg’s eltoo draft and executed within an Alice/Bob/Carol channel scenario, consistent with prior APO+CTV and CSFS+CTV ladder experiments. The process included publishing an outdated state, subsequently updating it with a new state signed before any prior state existed, and then settling the channel. A comprehensive write-up, including transaction details and a comparative analysis of all three implementations, is provided at [eltoo state chain on signet](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/eltoo-state-chain-on-signet-third-time-templatehash-csfs-internalkey/3012).
Through this implementation, several technical insights emerged. Using OP_TEMPLATEHASH offers a distinct advantage over CTV combined with CSFS by making the hash readily available on the stack, thereby allowing CSFS to sign the transaction directly. In contrast, using CTV required carrying an additional copy of the hash in the witness data, which complicates the construction. The Internal Key (IK) primarily serves to optimize byte usage, substituting a 32-byte key push and reducing the update script size to just 10 bytes. Importantly, CSFS on its own cannot bind the state, as it does not interact with the transaction directly; thus, OP_TEMPLATEHASH or a similar mechanism is necessary to provide the hash that CSFS needs for signing.
This progression in scripting reveals efficiencies in both transaction construction and state management for advanced Bitcoin protocols. The availability of detailed examples and comparisons assists developers in understanding the nuanced differences between various approaches, particularly as new opcodes like OP_TEMPLATEHASH become accessible for experimentation.
